_doc: The ladder of a run, stage by stage, as the progression bot played it (tests/tool_progress.gd, policy ladder; docs/audit/progression.md section 12 says how many runs, with which data and what the bot cannot do), read by scripts/sim/advisor.gd for the Ledger's goals ("p:<key>") and warnings. stages.<n> are the numbers at the END of stage n of the runs that went on to the next one: power_floor and power_median are Threat.power(ship, 0.75) at its best in the stage: the 25th percentile of the runs and their median (a ship that lost its power plant, under a quarter of the median, is left out); warden and enemy are the reference curve on the same scale: the mean power of the exit warden of the stage over every region it can be, and of a generated enemy at the middle of the stage (12.5 jumps a stage); guns (powered weapons), layers (shield layers), intakes (working intakes), plates (armour cells added to the starter's own), known (recipes known) are the median counts, never fewer than the stage before; fab is the fabricator level the ladder asks for (2 at stage 2, 3 from stage 3: the Assembly Rig and two arms in one room; the bot lays its workshop out in two rooms and never gets there, so this is the design's number, not the bot's); accel_ratio is the acceleration kept against the start (Threat.power's accel), the median, never above the stage before nor under warn.accel_min; fuel_margin is the fuel to spare over the jumps to the beacon (0 at stage 1, 2 after) and credits_over_toll the cushion over the warden's toll (0, then 40). warn: outgunned_ratio (power under this share of the stage's warden), skulls_ratio (a fight rated this much over you is 4 skulls), cliff_stage and cliff_power (the stage whose enemy budget jumps, and the power to have in it: that stage's power_floor), hull_left (the structure fraction under which the hull warning fires; the wreck line is 0.5), scrap_surplus (the 75th percentile of the scrap a ladder run holds at a stage end), accel_min (the 25th percentile of accel_ratio at a stage end) and known_stall (recipes known at the start of a run, plus one: a run that learned nothing).
